meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to drive out, depart', paired with 'выехать'.

выходить.gloss: to go out, to get out

meanings.en: to go out, to come out

examples.trans: I'm going out in a minute.

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'казать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to order', paired with 'заказывать'.

examples.text: Если опоздают, пицца бесплатно. Может, закажем?
examples.trans: If they're late, the pizza is free. Maybe we should order?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'hello'.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('intimate').
Чн is pronounced шн. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Делать массаж = to give a massage. Common masculine noun meaning 'massage' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна приказала сделать ей массаж ног!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna ordered me to give her a foot massage!

examples.text: А Клавдия Викторовна приказала сделать ей массаж ног!
examples.trans: And Klavdia Viktorovna ordered me to give her a foot massage!

meanings.note: Agent noun formed with the international suffix '-ист' denoting a specialist or adherent. Common masculine noun meaning 'massage therapist, masseur' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Наверное, массажист. Вика на столе визитку забыла.
examples.trans: Probably a masseur. Vika forgot the business card on the table.

examples.text: Что-то не похож он на массажиста! Ты сам говорил, что Вике секса хочется.
examples.trans: He does not look like a masseur! You said yourself that Vika wants sex.

examples.text: У нас напротив дома тоже написано массажный салон! И этот массажист сказал, что сделает Вике всё очень аккуратно!
examples.trans: Across from our house it also says massage parlor! And this masseur said he would do everything to Vika very carefully!

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('material, tangible').

examples.trans: They say that thoughts are material.

examples.text: Шеф говорит, что это очень материальный выбор.
examples.trans: The chef says that this is a very material choice.

meanings.note: Asking permission. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: Feminine noun (3rd declension). Common feminine noun meaning 'thought, idea' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: An interesting thought occurred to him.

examples.text: У меня была отличная умная мысль.
examples.trans: I had an excellent clever thought.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'терпение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'impatience' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I am waiting for you impatiently!

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть нетерпение.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always impatience.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (root 'терпенить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to forward'.

examples.text: Мы с нетерпением вновь ждём встречи с ним.
examples.trans: We eagerly look forward to meeting him again.
I am waiting for you impatiently!

meanings.note: Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.

meanings.note: A prisoner, a hand. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'пустить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to let go, to release', paired with 'отпускать'.

meanings.note: Colloquial, linking two things. Core Russian conj meaning 'plus' in everyday speech.
as a noun: это плюс = that's a plus

examples.trans: And I get you a suspended sentence. Plus you take all of Vika's money.

meanings.note: In a genuine and real manner.

+ в + prepositional. Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'знаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to confess, to admit', paired with 'признаваться'.

examples.text: Никак, я тебя на понт взяла. А ты сейчас сама призналась.
examples.trans: No way at all, I called your bluff. And you just confessed yourself.

meanings.note: usually 3rd person: что произошло? = what happened?

examples.text: Я не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: I don't know how it happened.

examples.text: Николай Филиппович, простите меня, пожалуйста. Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: Nikolai Filippovich, please forgive me. I don't know myself how it happened.

meanings.note: Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'dissolved, annulled'.

examples.trans: Now your marriage is officially dissolved.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и расторгнуть вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and dissolved on time.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'даваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to give up, to surrender', paired with 'сдаться'.

examples.text: Никогда не сдавайся! Сегодня я выйду отсюда под подписку!
examples.trans: Never give up! Today I'm getting out of here on a travel ban!

meanings.note: Reflexive; no nominative. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: As opposed to before. Core Russian adv meaning 'now (from now on)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.note: The one over there. Core Russian det meaning 'that' in everyday speech.
in 'то, что ...' = 'what, the thing that'
уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'service, favor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я такие важные услуги никогда не забываю.

examples.text: Потому что это настоящее кулинарное чудо!
